html:
Economic liberalisation in India is the set of reforms, begun in 1991, that opened the economy to foreign trade and investment and freed private business from tight state control.

Since independence India had run a planned economy. Businesses needed government licences to start, expand or import, a system mocked as the licence raj. In 1991, after years of deficits and the Gulf War oil shock, foreign reserves fell to about three weeks of imports. The government shipped gold to London as security for loans and turned to the International Monetary Fund.

Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and his finance minister Manmohan Singh used the crisis to act:

  • They devalued the rupee and cut import tariffs.
  • They scrapped most industrial licensing.
  • They let in foreign investment and opened sectors closed to private firms.

Growth sped up in the following decades, and software, telecoms and finance boomed; see the Bombay Stock Exchange. The reform came thirteen years after China's reform and opening, to which it is often compared.
sum: Economic liberalisation in India is the set of reforms, begun in 1991, that opened the economy to foreign trade and investment and freed private business from tight state control.
